sentence_of_record: TRACE-TRUNCATION (grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning, exact checker answer as reference, 360 MATH pairs over 185 questions, 2,178 calls): cutting the correct trace to its final line lowers the correct-verdict rate from 0.983 to 0.914 (drop 0.069 [0.039, 0.100], exact McNemar 26:1). The drop is almost entirely TIEs (order flips): 26 TIE + 5 wrong-side against 6 TIE + 0. The upper limit coincides with the 0.10 bar to within 0.0005 at every seed and estimator, so C1 is UNDETERMINED (descriptive by registration). The floor holds (C2 HELD, 0.914 [0.881, 0.947] against 0.70). Padding back with spaces costs more than truncation (-0.131 [-0.169, -0.092]), so the sensitivity reads as edit-sensitivity, not content-reading (C3). plain_description.what: The judge was given the exact correct final answer as a reference. The correct answer's reasoning was then cut down to its final line. The test checked whether verdicts change, using 360 MATH pairs and about 2,200 calls, with a control that pads the text back with spaces.
plain_description.why: It asks whether a judge with an exact reference just checks the outcome or still reacts to the reasoning text.
plain_description.information: No drop would make it an outcome judge. A drop would mean the reasoning still matters. Result: done. Accuracy fell from 0.983 to 0.914, mostly into ties rather than wrong verdicts. Whether this crosses the 0.10 bar is undetermined. The 0.70 floor held. Padding hurt even more, so the effect reads as sensitivity to edits, not to content. It is not shown to be an outcome judge.
